title: Never Split the Difference, lesson 1 - negotiation is emotional

slides.title: Think About Your Last Disagreement

graphic.title: In your last disagreement, did you...
graphic.note: Count the arguments on the left. Then the questions on the right.

body: When someone pushes back, most of us reach for **better arguments.**
Former FBI hostage negotiator **Chris Voss** learned that's usually the wrong move.

slides.title: Negotiation Was Taught Like Maths

graphic.q: Two calm calculators weighing offers. Ever met one?

body: For decades, negotiation was treated as a **rational problem.** The classic Harvard approach in _Getting to Yes_ said: separate the people from the problem.
Voss says this *misses how humans actually work.*

slides.title: Your Gut Answers Before Your Logic Does

graphic.label: QUICK, ANSWER IN 3 SECONDS
graphic.q:
A bat and a ball cost £1.10 in total.
The bat costs £1 more than the ball.
How much is the ball?
graphic.answer: answer: 5p, not the 10p your gut offered

body: Voss points to psychologist **Daniel Kahneman's** two systems:
System 1 reacts first. System 2 often just *explains the choice afterwards.*

slides.title: Without Feelings, You Can't Decide

graphic.q: Now choose using logic only. What actually decides it?

body: Neuroscientist **Antonio Damasio** studied people whose brain damage left them unable to feel emotions.
They could still reason, yet struggled with *even simple decisions.*
Feelings are what **tip the scales.**

slides.title: Who Would You Bet On?

graphic.q: Who wins more negotiations? Pick one, then swipe.

body: Voss once joined a negotiation course at **Harvard Law School.**
The students arrived armed with logic and tactics. Voss brought his crisis training: stay *curious* about what the other side feels and wants.

slides.title: Voss Won. Again And Again.
body: He outperformed the trained students **again and again.**
Fire facts at someone and their emotional brain *digs in.* Listening lowers their guard.
Once you know what they **fear and hope for**, you know what will move them.

slides.title: This Is Tactical Empathy

graphic.q: Where did you land in your last argument?

body: Voss calls it _tactical empathy_: understanding the other side's feelings, and **showing them you understand.**
It's not agreeing. It's not being soft. People say yes to those who *make them feel understood.*

slides.title: Before Your Next Tough Conversation

graphic.title: THE 2-MINUTE PREP
graphic.total: Start there. Not with your argument.

body: Set your arguments aside for a moment. **Screenshot this.**
Write down what they might be feeling, and what they might be *afraid of losing.*

slides.title: One Question To Sit With

graphic.q: In your next disagreement, will you try to win the argument, or understand the person?

body: People don't decide with logic first. **They decide with feelings.**
Save this, and follow for lesson 2. Full animated lesson at *visualgrowth.app*
